brief.headline: Continuity Guardian could not produce a grounded review
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 997140 (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting, idle in transaction, txn open 4.2s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 0% over 30s (120/120 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $18,400/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting, pid 997140) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $18,400/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: Root blocker pid 997140 (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting) is idle in transaction for 4.2s with last statement SELECT 1, holding locks without active work (DB-1). Checkout success is 55-77% (TEL-1, BIZ-1) vs 95% SLO with $4,293-$18,400/min revenue at risk and only 60s business tolerance (BIZ-1, BIZ-4). No protected settlements in flight (DB-2). adhoc_reporting is NOT FOUND in workload registry (BIZ-2) — unknown owner, replayability, and interrupt cost — and no change-calendar window protects it (BIZ-3). Trade-off is unknown due to missing registry entry (BIZ-5). Memory shows terminating a similar batch workload (batch_replayable_inventory) previously restored checkout to 100% (MEM-1). Given the blocker is idle, checkout is severely degraded, business tolerance is nearly exhausted, and no protections exist for this workload, termination is the lowest-blast-radius action to restore checkout.

audit.report: An adhoc_reporting batch worker (pid 997140) sat idle in transaction for 4.2 seconds holding locks, blocking 12 sessions and dropping checkout success to 0–77% against a 95% SLO with $4,293–$18,400/min revenue at risk. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the blocker, citing memory that a similar batch termination previously restored checkout to 100%. The Continuity Guardian could not produce a grounded review after two attempts, triggering escalation to on-call after 225 seconds with no action executed. The business tolerance of 60 seconds was exceeded before a decision could be enacted.
audit.root_cause: An unregistered adhoc_reporting batch workload held locks idle-in-transaction, blocking checkout and exceeding the 60-second degradation tolerance.
lessons: Register adhoc_reporting in the workload registry with owner, criticality, and interrupt cost so the Continuity Guardian can ground trade-offs instantly instead of finding 'NOT FOUND'.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian acted on evidence in one round, proposing and confirming terminate with telemetry, business, and memory citations. The Continuity Guardian wasted no round but failed grounding twice on the same missing registry entry, causing the pact to fail closed and escalate without a decision.
follow_ups: Add adhoc_reporting to the workload registry with defined owner, SLA tier, and safe-interrupt procedure.
Implement a watchdog that kills idle-in-transaction batch workers exceeding 2s on the checkout critical path.
Provide the Continuity Guardian a 'unknown workload, revenue at risk' grounding playbook to prevent double grounding failure.
